answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce token deposit before voting, with deposits slashable when later evidence proves coordinated fake identities. A river of accounts then offers no free influence: every extra identity needs its own capital, and detection destroys that stake rather than merely banning an account. A zephyr of cheap account creation becomes expensive when each account must risk real value; a sonnet-like pattern of identical claims can trigger review, but similarity alone should not prove fraud, since honest agents may share information.
